requirement:
After a rejection under {cite}`requirements.authoring.line_numbers.rejection`,
a submission whose previously flagged rationale is exactly the UUID that rejection gave MUST
resolve to the rejected submission unchanged, ignoring the new submission's
other fields; acceptance remains subject to
{cite}`requirements.authoring.submission.searches.line_numbers`. After passing that gate, any other rationale that cites line numbers MUST fail
the assessment, so
an assessment rejects at most one submission. The UUID MUST NOT be recorded in
evidence.
rationale:
I judged the tests against the text of `requirements.authoring.line_numbers.resubmission`. I did not read implementation source. The reviewed tests cover every obligation I derived.

**1. Exactly the UUID resolves to the rejected submission unchanged, ignoring the other fields.**
- `src/authoring/line_numbers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_rejection_gives_a_uuid_that_keeps_the_rejected_submission]` rejects a submission with `determination: false` and a line-number rationale. It then resubmits `determination: true` with the rationale set to the UUID. It asserts that `resubmitted` returns exactly the original `cited` value, so the differing determination is ignored.
- The same test asserts that the UUID followed by a trailing space returns `None`, which checks the "exactly" clause.
- It also asserts that a UUID submitted before any rejection does not resolve.
- `src/authoring/line_numbers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[uuid_restores_only_at_the_rejected_correction_position]` covers the `Failed` form. The UUID at corrections position 0 gives `None`. The UUID at position 1 with an empty correction at position 0 returns the original submission.

**2. Acceptance remains subject to the outstanding-search gate.**
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[keeping_a_rejected_rationale_waits_for_search_and_preserves_the_original_verdict]` runs end to end. After the rejection, the model starts a search, then tries to keep the rationale with the UUID while the search is outstanding. The test asserts that the reply tells the model to call `finish_search`.
- After `finish_search`, the second keep succeeds.
- The test asserts that the request count is 5, so the first keep did not finish the assessment.

**3. After the gate, any other rationale that cites line numbers fails, so at most one rejection happens.**
- The first test asserts that a clean resubmission is accepted. It asserts that a second line-number-citing submission gets `Outcome::Fail` with a message containing "after a rejection".
- The second test asserts `Outcome::Fail` for a repeat of the original submission after the UUID was used.

**4. The UUID is not recorded in evidence.**
- The CLI test reads the evidence file and asserts that the determination is `true`, that the rationale equals the original text, and that the record does not contain the UUID.

The fresh-UUID property belongs to the `rejection` requirement. It is also checked in the first test, which asserts that a second `Rejection` produces a different UUID. The cited `requirements.authoring.submission.searches.line_numbers` obligation, that a search rejection leaves the correction attempt available, is exercised by the CLI test, because the keep still works after the search gate blocked it.

All three tests carry `{test}` references to the subject.

For requirement, example, and site reviews, when the only submission in a response
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.submission` is otherwise valid but any of its
rationales cites line numbers under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.line_numbers.detection`, and it is the
assessment's first such submission, and it passes the outstanding-search gate
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.submission.searches.line_numbers`, the
harness MUST reject it instead of
accepting it and continue the conversation. The tool result MUST quote the
matched text, identify the affected rationale (including its correction position
for `Failed`), repeat the location guidance of
{cite}`requirements.authoring.judgment_rules`, and give a fresh random UUID,
saying the model may submit once more, either without line numbers or with
the offending rationale set to exactly that UUID to keep the rejected submission as it was.
A rejection MUST be counted in usage like any other turn.
:::{req} submission.searches.line_numbers

The SDK checks for outstanding searches before invoking Habeas's rationale vetting. A submission rejected for an outstanding search MUST leave the rationale correction attempt available under {cite}`requirements.authoring.line_numbers.rejection`.
